F001.acceptance: (1) A delivers item with proof.method walk and a metric >=10 validates. (2) proof.method 'kpi_warehouse' is rejected by both JSON Schema and Pydantic. (3) A fixture plan with inherits set and a one-item delta delivers[] validates. (4) Existing plans without proof keep their current validation exit code. (5) The subtree-pulled schema matches agent-conventions.

F002.acceptance: (1) Lock of a fixture with no delivers, no inherits, and no proof-carrying feature fails with a message that names 'outcome'. (2) Lock of a fixture that inherits a parent and declares one delta slice succeeds. (3) Lock of a fixture whose features each carry a proof and which declares no delivers[] SUCCEEDS, scoring one slice per proof-carrying feature. (4) A feature-as-slice with no user_impact locks successfully and records an accepted gap naming the absent audience. (5) Lock of a fixture with outcome and an accepted missing proof succeeds and records the gap. (6) Existing plans without proof still lock (inferred or accepted-gap, never a surprise refuse). (7) The outcome-score suite passes and the run is evidenced with real command output, not an empty commands_run.

F003.acceptance: (1) README states that every locked plan names an outcome, slices, and a proof, and that a fix inherits. (2) README does not claim intake or PRD authoring. (3) CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased or dated entry. (4) The new block is shorter than the existing Why-not-just-Claude-Code section.

F004.acceptance: (1) Replacing a locked slice with a different feature at the same numeric index keeps the locked obligation AND surfaces the live slice as its own obligation. (2) Prepending a slice, and separately reordering slices, each leave every locked obligation intact. (3) A test asserts close_obligations() does not key on index — mutating only the index of a live slice must not change the obligation set. (4) A cross-plan proof ref 'parent:F001' is satisfied only by evidence on F001 of plan 'parent'; a local F001 with matching evidence does NOT satisfy it. (5) Two slices naming the same proving features but differing in capability text, swapped in order, produce byte-identical obligations and report NO drift — each locked record pairs with the live slice carrying its own capability. (6) Two slices identical in both proving features and capability are documented as interchangeable; a reorder of those is a no-op, and the code says why rather than implying a distinction it cannot make.

F005.acceptance: (1) A plan locked before the sidecar artifact existed still closes as it does today (no surprise refuse). (2) A deleted or corrupt outcome-score.json on a plan that WAS locked with one is distinguishable from case 1 and behaves differently at close; the chosen semantics are recorded in decisions.jsonl. (3) Lock never exits zero while reporting that gaps were not recorded: either the score is persisted before the status flip, or status stays draft and the exit code is nonzero, proven by a write-failure test.
